summary:
The built part of SL-101 is criterion 1: a never-throw Controlled Folder Access (CFA) record line written beside the fsutil line. It does what the design's 14 criteria say, and I checked each one by running something.

**On this PC (HEAD d79ce14)**
- The whole suite passed 870 of 870, with 0 skipped, exit 0 and TEMP=%LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp. Fitness reports 91 rules, all holding.
- Every one of the 6 HeldOpenTree Facts prints the fsutil line, and on the next line 'Controlled Folder Access: EnableControlledFolderAccess=0 (Disabled), protected folders=0, allowed apps=hidden from non-administrators; Defender AMRunningMode=Normal, RealTimeProtection=True, platform=4.18.26080.4'.
- A separate Windows PowerShell 5.1 read of EnableControlledFolderAccess, done by me outside the tests, gives 0.
- testhost inherits pwsh 7's PSModulePath. The child reports only its own three Windows PowerShell entries.
- **New measurement for criterion 13, which the build left untested:** I loaded the built test DLL and had 8 threads read DefenderState.Line at once. All 8 got the same string instance. They finished in 658 ms, about one read (a fresh read takes 548 ms), and a later call took 0 ms. So the line is computed once per process, even with parallel callers.

**In a Windows Sandbox with Defender disabled** (AMRunningMode 'Not running', Get-MpPreference fails with 0x800106ba)
- All 65 DefenderStateRecordTests passed against the same build output.
- The real line read 'Controlled Folder Access: not read (Get-MpPreference : Operation failed with the following error: 0x800106ba)'.
- The fresh-read agreement Fact took its not-read branch and passed. So on a PC without Defender, the default suite does not turn red because of this record.
- The timeout Fact returned in 1028 ms. After that run, the only powershell.exe processes left were the Sandbox's own two, so the 30 s sleeper had been killed.
- The six HeldOpenTree Facts could not run there. Their fixture refuses SYSTEM's temp folder (TempTree.ChooseTestsRoot), and that file was not changed by this slice. So HeldOpenTreeTests.Record() itself was not seen on a machine without Defender. It reads the same static Lazy as the Facts that did pass there.

**Not done: criteria 2 and 3 and Q-101**
- Nobody has scanned a CFA-protected folder with CFA in AuditMode or Enabled, read 1123/1124 events, or watched for a notification.
- That needs an administrator to arm CFA and a person at the desktop, and the Sandbox cannot run Defender (measured again here).
- Both are graded person-run against the recipe in docs/design/SL-101-controlled-folder-access.md.
- O-014, O-015 and O-016 are owed to this stage. They are preconditions of that person's run, so I cannot tell whether they hold.
- For O-016 I read: no CFA Group Policy key exists, and Tamper Protection is on. Whether Tamper Protection stops Set-MpPreference is unmeasured; the recipe has a Windows Security UI fallback.

**Index**
- One build attempt, not sent back, and no loop.
- The waived minors (O-025, O-028, O-029) are on the backlog, and I found nothing new.

checks.what: Whole suite as the project runs it
checks.evidence: Passed! Failed: 0, Passed: 870, Skipped: 0, Total: 870 (FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.dll, net10.0). Exit 0, 27.5 s. TEMP=C:\Users\sshub\AppData\Local\Temp. HEAD d79ce14.

checks.what: Architecture rules (Fitness), including SL-101's new rule 'no test or test script changes Microsoft Defender's settings'
checks.evidence: 91 rules checked against 161 parsed files: every declared rule holds.

checks.what: Criterion 1 in real use: HeldOpenTree output and DefenderStateRecordTests, detailed logger
checks.evidence:
71 tests, exit 0.
- 6 pairs of lines: 'fsutil behavior query disablelastaccess: exit 0: DisableLastAccess = 2 (System Managed, Last Access Time Updates ENABLED)', then on the next line 'Controlled Folder Access: EnableControlledFolderAccess=0 (Disabled), protected folders=0, allowed apps=hidden from non-administrators; Defender AMRunningMode=Normal, RealTimeProtection=True, platform=4.18.26080.4'.
- testhost PSModulePath contains 'c:\program files\powershell\7\Modules'; the child's PSModulePath is OneDrive\Documents\WindowsPowerShell\Modules;C:\Program Files\WindowsPowerShell\Modules;C:\WINDOWS\system32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\Modules.
- Fresh read: exit 0, said '0'.
- Timeout Fact returned after 1036 ms with 'not read (timed out after 1 s)'.
- Missing exe gave 'not read (Win32Exception: ...)'.

checks.what: Independent fresh read of the CFA setting, outside the test code
checks.evidence: 0, in 548 ms. This matches the record's 'EnableControlledFolderAccess=0 (Disabled)'.

checks.what: Criterion 13, first attempt: 8 parallel callers of DefenderState.Line through PowerShell scriptblocks on Task.Run
checks.evidence: My probe was wrong: PowerShell scriptblocks have no runspace on thread-pool threads ('There is no Runspace available'). Nothing was measured. I redid it in compiled C# (next check).

checks.what: Criterion 13: the line is computed once per process when 8 callers ask in parallel
checks.command: Add-Type C# LazyProbe: Assembly.LoadFrom(FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.dll), 8 LongRunning tasks released by one gate, each reads DefenderState.Line by reflection; then compare ReferenceEquals and elapsed time
checks.evidence: 8 parallel callers took 658 ms, about one 5.1 read (548 ms measured separately). All 8 got the same string instance and there was 1 distinct text. A later call took 0 ms and returned the same instance. powershell.exe count was 2 before and 2 after, so no child was left behind.

checks.what: Defender context for O-016 and as an outside view of the setting: Tamper Protection, CFA policy key, CFA registry value, CFA events
checks.command: Get-MpComputerStatus IsTamperProtected; Get-ItemProperty HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\...\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Controlled Folder Access and HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Controlled Folder Access; Get-WinEvent Defender Operational Id 1123,1124 (+5007 mentioning CFA)
checks.evidence:
Read-only, nothing changed.
- IsTamperProtected=True; AMRunningMode=Normal.
- The CFA policy key does not exist (ItemNotFoundException), so no GPO sets CFA.
- The non-policy key exists with EnableControlledFolderAccess unset (default off).
- 0 CFA events.

checks.what: Criteria 9-12 on a real Windows without Defender: DefenderStateRecordTests in Windows Sandbox
checks.command: Sandbox (SYSTEM, network off): C:\taad\tree\.dotnet\dotnet.exe vstest FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.dll /TestCaseFilter:"FullyQualifiedName~DefenderStateRecordTests|FullyQualifiedName~HeldOpenTree" /logger:console;verbosity=detailed (bin copied to C:\work)
checks.evidence:
Sandbox Defender: AMRunningMode=Not running; Get-MpPreference fails with 0x800106ba.
- 65 of 65 DefenderStateRecordTests passed.
- Real line: 'Controlled Folder Access: not read (Get-MpPreference : Operation failed with the following error: 0x800106ba)'.
- TheLineAgreesWithAFreshReadOnThisPc took its not-read branch (fresh read exit 1) and passed.
- Timeout Fact: 1028 ms. Missing exe: Win32Exception line.
- After the run, only 2 powershell.exe were left, and the second Sandbox run shows those 2 are the Sandbox harness's own (run.ps1 and its host). So the Start-Sleep 30 child of the timeout Fact was gone within the ~19 s run.

checks.what: HeldOpenTreeTests (where Record() prints the line) in Windows Sandbox as SYSTEM
checks.command: same Sandbox vstest run, HeldOpenTree part
checks.evidence: 6 of 6 failed in 1 ms with 'Class fixture type HeldOpenTreeTests+HeldOpenTree threw in its constructor'. The cause is TempTree.ChooseTestsRoot (TempTree.cs:69): '%TEMP% (C:\Windows\SystemTemp\) is under the Windows folder ... this process runs under a system or service profile'. TempTree.cs is not in this slice's diff (git diff 9851b9c..HEAD touches only DefenderState*, HeldOpenTreeTests.cs:132-137, the doc and fitness.yaml). The refusal comes from SL-096. It fails before Record() is reached, so it says nothing about the record.

checks.what: Retry of HeldOpenTree in Sandbox with TEMP/TMP pointed at C:\work\tmp
checks.evidence: Same fixture refusal, 6 of 6. For a SYSTEM process the temp path still resolves to C:\Windows\SystemTemp\ whatever TEMP says. So in this Sandbox, Record() cannot be watched printing the 'not read' line beside fsutil. Running as a local user was not tried: build-check found net user stops at a password-length prompt.

checks.what: Scope of the change and the opt-in machinery (criterion 14)
checks.evidence:
Changed files:
- added: DefenderState.cs, DefenderStateRecordTests.cs, DefenderStateCorpus.json, docs/design/SL-101-controlled-folder-access.md, plus the slice records
- edited: HeldOpenTreeTests.cs (+1 line `output.WriteLine(DefenderState.Line);` after the fsutil line, and a comment); fitness.yaml (+1 settled rule over tests/**)

No csproj, filter, Trait or src/ file was touched. The new class has no Trait, Skip or Explicit, and runs in the default 870.

checks.what: Criteria 2 and 3: scan a CFA-protected folder with CFA in AuditMode or Enabled; record block/fallback, 1123/1124 events and notifications
checks.evidence: Arming CFA needs an administrator, and only a person can see a notification. The Sandbox cannot run Defender: confirmed again in my run (AMRunningMode 'Not running', 0x800106ba), and build-check measured WinDefend DISABLED, error 1058, and error 5 even as SYSTEM. Neither engine elevation operation (whoami, read-denied-folders) can arm CFA. Graded person-run.

criteria.criterion: 1. Record the CFA state beside the fsutil state when CFA is off on a PC where Defender is running (this PC: EnableControlledFolderAccess=0)
criteria.how: Ran on this PC: every HeldOpenTree Fact prints 'Controlled Folder Access: EnableControlledFolderAccess=0 (Disabled), ...' on the line directly after the fsutil disablelastaccess line. An independent 5.1 read gives 0, and the CFA registry value is unset (default off). The whole suite passed 870 of 870.

criteria.criterion: 2. Record the CFA state beside the fsutil state when testhost was launched from pwsh 7 (eng/dotnet.ps1) and inherits pwsh 7's PSModulePath
criteria.how: Under eng/dotnet.ps1, testhost's PSModulePath contains c:\program files\powershell\7\Modules. The child reports only its own three Windows PowerShell paths, and the record line was read successfully.

criteria.criterion: 3. Count the protected-folder list when it is empty and serialises as JSON null
criteria.how: ANullOrEmptyListCountsAsZero (null and []) and corpus rows R01/R02 passed in the 870 and in the Sandbox. On this PC the live line reads 'protected folders=0'.

criteria.criterion: 4. Count a list that arrives as a single JSON string
criteria.how: AScalarListCountsAsOneNotAsItsLength and corpus rows R03/P02 passed on this PC and in the Sandbox.

criteria.criterion: 5. Count a list that is an array of several entries
criteria.how: AnArrayListCountsItsLength (1, 2 and 3 entries) and corpus rows R05/R08 passed. The live allowed-apps placeholder reads 'hidden from non-administrators', not 1.

criteria.criterion: 6. Name the CFA mode when EnableControlledFolderAccess=2 (AuditMode)
criteria.how: TheModeIsNamedAndTheRawValueKept (0-4, with 2 giving 'AuditMode') passed. This is fixed-input only: no live value of 2 was ever read, because CFA was never armed.

criteria.criterion: 7. Name the CFA mode when the value is a number outside 0..4
8. Record the Defender run state when a property is missing from the JSON
criteria.how: AMissingPropertyPrintsAQuestionMarkAndTheRestOfTheLineStays passed. A key the cmdlet lacks serialises as null rather than missing (O-026, waived to SC-280), and the null arm is not fed by any test.

criteria.criterion: 9. Record without failing the test when the child exits non-zero with stderr (Defender not running, Sandbox 0x800106ba, third-party AV)
criteria.how: Real environment: in a Windows Sandbox with Defender disabled the line read 'Controlled Folder Access: not read (Get-MpPreference : Operation failed with the following error: 0x800106ba)', and all 65 DefenderStateRecordTests passed, including the fresh-read agreement Fact. A third-party antivirus was not tried.

criteria.criterion: 10. Record without failing when stdout is empty or not JSON
criteria.how: EmptyOrUnparsedOutputIsNotRead (9 rows) and NullOutputIsNotReadEither passed. A lone surrogate is still able to throw out of Describe (O-029, waived to SC-284); ReadOnce's catch-all covers it.

criteria.criterion: 11. Record without failing when the child runs past the timeout
criteria.how: With a real Start-Sleep 30 child and a 1 s timeout, the call returned in 1036 ms on this PC and 1028 ms in the Sandbox, with 'not read (timed out after 1 s)'. After the Sandbox run, no powershell.exe remained beyond the harness's own two.

criteria.criterion: 12. Record without failing when the executable cannot be started
criteria.how: AnExecutableThatCannotBeStartedIsNotRead gave 'not read (Win32Exception: An error occurred trying to start process ...)' on this PC and in the Sandbox.

criteria.criterion: 13. Record the CFA state once per test process when several HeldOpenTree Facts ask, possibly in parallel
criteria.how: Measured by me (the build left it untested): 8 threads released together read DefenderState.Line from the built DLL. They took 658 ms, about one 548 ms read, and all got the same string instance. A later call took 0 ms.

criteria.criterion: 14. Keep the default suite's opt-in machinery intact when DefenderStateRecordTests joins Core.Tests
criteria.how: No csproj, filter or Trait was changed (git diff). The class has no Trait or Skip. The whole suite passed 870 of 870 with 0 skipped, including OptInTraitTests and CountingRuleTestsAreNeverSkipped. Fitness: 91 rules hold.

criteria.criterion: Derived criterion 2 (build-check): a scan of a CFA-protected folder is run with CFA on and the outcome recorded (keep-open/LastAccessTime=-1 blocked or not; listed in full; kept or fell back)
criteria.how:
A person follows docs/design/SL-101-controlled-folder-access.md steps 1-10.
- W-admin (Run as administrator) only reads state, arms and disarms: step 1 Get-MpPreference with both lists by name; step 5 Set-MpPreference -EnableControlledFolderAccess AuditMode plus Add-MpPreference for $base\R-audit and $base\R-on; step 7 Enabled; step 9 restore.
- W-user (ordinary window, the step 3 guard must print Medium Mandatory Level) does everything else: runs A, B and C with Witness, Scan, Witness, Control, Canary, Events.

What it must show, filled into the results table:
- Baseline A: Witness 'unchanged' before and after; Control 'moved'; canary exit 0; 15 files / 1 folder / 6280 bytes / 0 unreadable.
- B and C: the canary is refused or audited, with an event naming its folder; otherwise the row is void.
- For the scan: Witness 'unchanged' means kept, not blocked. 'MOVED' with a 1123 naming FsAnalyser.App.exe means blocked and fell back, and files/folders/bytes must still equal the baseline with unreadable 0. Anything short of the baseline is a defect slice.

criteria.criterion: Derived criterion 3 (build-check): whether such a scan raises a CFA block/audit event or a user-visible notification is recorded
criteria.how:
In the same session, after runs B (AuditMode) and C (Enabled), the person records:
- what the Events helper prints: 1123 (blocked) and 1124 (audited) lines naming FsAnalyser.App.exe, fsa-cfa-canary.exe or the fsa-cfa- folder. If nothing prints but the canary was refused, the whole newest 1123/1124 message.
- whether a Windows Security notification appeared during the scan, and its text, kept apart from the canary's own toast.

That result answers Q-101.

obligations.evidence: O-014 says CFA judges the unsigned published single-file exe rather than testhost or dotnet. Only CFA in AuditMode or Enabled could show which image it acts on, through the 'Process Name:' line of a 1123/1124 event. Arming needs an administrator, and the Sandbox cannot run Defender (confirmed in my Sandbox run: AMRunningMode 'Not running', Get-MpPreference 0x800106ba). This precondition belongs to the person's recipe, not to shipped code, and it is checked inside that run (steps 6/8, Events). Design-slice imported it as a validate obligation, although it is person-gated (O-027, waived to SC-281).

O-015 says a custom protected folder is judged like Documents, Desktop and Pictures. It needs CFA armed by an administrator. Unreachable here for the same reason as O-014. The recipe still uses custom folders under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp. The C:\Users\Public\Documents fixture that would make this hold by construction was waived to SC-275 (O-020). Only the person's run, or a run on the default-protected Public\Documents, can settle it.

O-016 says the person can arm CFA by cmdlet or through the Windows Security UI.

Measured unelevated, read-only:
- HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Controlled Folder Access does not exist, so no Group Policy would override the cmdlet.
- Get-MpComputerStatus IsTamperProtected=True.

Whether Tamper Protection refuses Set-MpPreference -EnableControlledFolderAccess is unmeasured: it needs an administrator, which no engine elevation operation provides. The recipe's step 5 gives the Windows Security UI fallback for Enabled, and says AuditMode is then skipped.

not_reached: A scan of a CFA-protected folder with CFA in AuditMode or Enabled. Whether the FILE_LIST_DIRECTORY|FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES keep-open and the LastAccessTime=-1 set are refused, whether the folder is still listed in full, and whether it is counted as kept or fell back (derived criterion 2, Q-101). It needs an administrator to arm CFA, and the Sandbox cannot run Defender.
Whether such a scan raises a 1123/1124 event or a visible Windows Security notification (derived criterion 3). Only a person at the desktop can see a toast.

Which image CFA judges (the unsigned published exe), whether a custom protected folder is treated like Documents, and whether Tamper Protection (on, on this PC) refuses Set-MpPreference for CFA (O-014, O-015, O-016).

HeldOpenTreeTests.Record() printing the 'not read' line beside fsutil on a Windows without Defender. In the Sandbox the HeldOpenTree fixture refuses SYSTEM's temp folder (pre-existing TempTree rule), so only DefenderStateRecordTests' reads of the same Lazy line were seen there.

PCs where Defender runs in Passive, SxS Passive or EDR Block mode, an older platform, or a third-party antivirus. The fresh-read agreement Fact may go red there (O-025, waived to SC-282); not measured.
Whether ControlledFolderAccessProtectedFolders becomes the 'N/A:' placeholder for a non-administrator once it is non-empty. It is empty on this PC.
The branch where the write-attributes open succeeds but SetFileInformationByHandle(FileBasicInfo) fails. Neither spike #109 nor this slice exercises it.
Windows 10, and Defender platforms other than 4.18.26080.4 (Q-205, Q-224).
